chunks: Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Ahmad ibn Yunus al-Mu'adhi narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id al-Kufi al-Hamdani narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Fadl narrated to us, from his father, who said: I asked al-Rida, Ali ibn Musa (peace be upon them), about the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He:
"No! Verily, they are, from their Lord, on that Day, indeed, obstructed"

He said: Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, is not characterized by a place in which He is embodied and in which His servants will be obstructed from Him, however, He, Exalted and Glorious is He, means that they will be, from the reward of their Lord, obstructed.

And I asked him about the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: "And your Lord came, and the Angels, rows after rows." He said: Indeed, Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He, is not characterized by coming and going. Exalted is He above movement. He only means by that: "And the commandment of your Lord came, and the Angels, rows after rows."

And I asked him about the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: "Do they wait but that Allah will come to them in shadows of clouds, and so the Angels." He said: He says: "Do they wait but that Allah will bring to them Angels in shadows of clouds." This is how it was revealed.

And I asked him about the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: "Allah ridiculed them" and about His saying: "Allah derides them" and about His saying: "And they plotted, and Allah plotted" and about His saying: "They attempt to deceive Allah, whilst He deceives them." He said: Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, does not ridicule, nor mock, nor plot, nor deceive, however, Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He, will reward them with the reward of ridiculing, and the reward of mocking, and the reward of plotting, and the reward of deception. Exalted is Allah above what the wrongdoers say, a Great Highness.
ai.seo_question: How does Imam al-Rida explain the literal vs. metaphorical meaning of divine attributes like 'coming' and 'plotting' in the Quran?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Mani al-Akhbar*, Imam al-Rida elucidates the Shia doctrine of *Tanzih* (divine transcendence) by interpreting anthropomorphic Quranic terms as metaphors for divine action rather than physical attributes. He clarifies that 'obstruction' refers to being veiled from reward, 'coming' signifies the arrival of divine command, and 'mocking' or 'plotting' denote the execution of justice implies the bestowal of corresponding recompense, thereby preserving Allah's freedom from physical location, movement, or human-like emotions.

en.basel-kadem: 3.	We were told by Muhammed bin Ibrahim bin Ahmad bin Yunus al-Mu’adhi, that he said: We were told by Ahmad bin Muhammed bin Sa’eed al-Kufi al-Hamdani, that he said: We were told by Ali bin Hasan bin Faddal, from his father, that he said: I asked al-Rida, Ali bin Musa, peace be upon him, about the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He:
«No! Verily, they are, from their Lord, on that Day, indeed, obstructed» [83:15]

to which he said: Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, is not characterized by a place in which He is embodied and in which His servants will be obstructed from Him, however, He, Exalted and Glorious is He, means that they will be, from the reward of their Lord, obstructed.

Also, I asked him about the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: «And your Lord came, and the Angels, rows after rows» [89:23] to which he said: Indeed, Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He, is not characterized by coming and going. Exalted is He above movement. He only means by that: And the commandment of your Lord came, and the Angels, rows after rows.

Also, I asked him about the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: «Do they wait but that Allah will come to them in shadows of clouds, and so the Angels» [2:210]. He said: He says: «Do they wait but that Allah will bring to them Angels in shadows of clouds.» [1] This is how it was revealed.

Also, I asked him about the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: «Allah ridiculed them» [9:78] and about His saying: «Allah derides them» [2:15] and about His saying: «And they plotted, and Allah plotted» [3:54] and about His saying: «They attempt to deceive Allah, whilst He deceives them» [4:142] to which he said: Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, does not ridicule, nor mock, nor plot, nor deceive, however, Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He, will reward them with the reward of ridiculing, and the reward of mocking, and the reward of plotting, and the reward of deception. Exalted is Allah above what the wrongdoers say, a Great Highness.
